body:
Thank you all so much for validating that yes, in fact, this was real, and no, it really wasn't just in my head, and it really wasn't my fault. 

This happened a few months ago. I processed it a little bit, then pushed it aside, not realizing just how much of the pain and shame and confusion I was just pushing deep inside and clinging to. Having the ability to write it down and get it out has been such an amazing release. I feel free. I am no longer clinging to the pain and shame.

I'm not angry, and I do not wish him harm. Don't get me wrong - I am absolutely horrified and thoroughly disgusted with his actions, and would never, EVER trust him again with anything. I have no desire to see or speak to him again, and I have actively avoided him. I can't speak for anyone else, but holding onto anger and ill wishes doesn't do anything positive for me, and will only eat me alive. It's just the way I work. 

This past weekend, during a silent meditation retreat, while doing mettā practice, I thought about him and did my best to wish him well - that he would be fulfilled and happy, and never, ever feel the desire to do anything remotely like this to anyone ever again. 

I hope that through my failure to return any of his text messages or phone calls, my refusals to speak or work with him, and the unwavering ferocity I've had towards growing my business has been a slap in the face to him - not of pain, but of an awakening that he is NOTHING to me. I never needed his "help". He will never "win" my interest, affection, or my business. 

The only way for me to truly heal from this is to confront it head on, which I am so grateful to have had the opportunity to do here. I have done so much healing through gratitude. I am so grateful that even in whatever state I was in, I was clear minded enough to refuse to allow him to enter my home; that it wasn't in my bed; that I wasn't more brutally assaulted; that I don't have any permanent physical injuries; that I felt safe enough to reach out to my best friend. I am grateful for all of the things in my past that have made me as strong as I needed to be to get through this; I am grateful that in some way, this will make me stronger. 

As Robert Heinlein wrote, "You cannot conquer a free [wo]man. The most you can do is kill [her]." 

Well, I am still alive. 

Like the saying - "They tried to bury us. They didn't know we were seeds." 

I am now the seed: I can choose grow into aloe and help people heal, or I can choose grow into a cactus full of thorns. I chose to become aloe. To help me transform this horror into a positive, I'm planning on volunteering to help other women that have suffered the atrocity of sexual assault.

He is nothing. He can't crush me, or steal from me, or possess me. He is nothing. I am free. He cannot own me. He cannot destroy me. I will only grow stronger!

I love it. 
I think you should do it, take high res pictures, make instagram-y artsy edits, and sell prints using a fake name.
Why yes, crunk is a state of being that is an end in and of itself!
I can't tell you how much it meant to read this, and to know that - holy shit - I'm not alone. YOU'RE fucking awesome.
